proposedOverrides.summary: East Germany, the German Democratic Republic, existed from 7 October 1949 to 3 October 1990. The imported 1960 to 1994 map interval begins late and ends after reunification. SED rule restricted elections and travel, while work, childcare, prefab homes, school clubs and holiday camps shaped everyday life. Indoor bathrooms and medical care differed across homes and years. Peaceful protest and a free 1990 election led to the GDR joining the Federal Republic; its people and family histories continued.

proposedOverrides.summary: West Germany refers to the Federal Republic of Germany during the 1949 to 1990 division. Its Basic Law, parliament and statutory health insurance shaped a democracy that continued after unification. Postwar housing shortages gave way to construction and consumer goods for many, though gains were unequal. Migrant workers and their families also built West German society. In 1990 the GDR joined the Federal Republic: the Cold War name West Germany ended, but the Federal Republic did not.
